en.title: Redeemed, How I Love to Proclaim It
en.author: Fanny J. Crosby
stanzas:
Re[G]deemed, how I love to proclaim it!
Re[D]deemed by the blood of the [G]Lamb;
Re[G]deemed through His infinite mercy,
His [D7]child and forever I [G]am.

Redeemed, and so happy in Jesus,
No language my rapture can tell;
I know that the light of His presence
With me doth continually dwell.

I think of my blessed Redeemer,
I think of Him all the day long:
I sing, for I cannot be silent;
His love is the theme of my song.

I know I shall see in His beauty
The King in whose law I delight;
Who lovingly guardeth my footsteps,
And giveth me songs in the night.

I know there's a crown that is waiting
In yonder bright mansion for me,
And soon, with the spirits made perfect,
At home with the Lord I shall be.
en.chorus:
Re[C]deemed, re[G]deemed,
Re[D]deemed by the blood of the [G]Lamb;
Re[C]deemed, re[G]deemed,
His [D7]child and forever I [G]am.

notes: Text from Timeless Truths, which cites the Cyber Hymnal's transcription of Songs of Redeeming Love (Philadelphia 1882); the two agree word for word (the Cyber Hymnal marks 'blessèd'). Five stanzas; hymnary's representative text (Our Great Redeemer's Praise #530) prints four, dropping the last ('I know there's a crown'), and differs only in punctuation. All five ship. Tune: hymnary names it REDEEMED (Kirkpatrick); some hymnals call it ADA. Meter 9.8.9.8 with refrain. Key: hymnary's instances run 32 A-flat to 2 G and 2 A; TT prints A-flat. Moved to G for guitar per the key rule. Chords derived from the Timeless Truths MusicXML score by reading the four-part chord on every beat, transposed A-flat to G. The score is an echo setting ('redeemed, redeemed' answered in the lower voices); its harmony is I with IV/G and sus4 neighbours over the pedal (dropped), V on 'by the blood' with a ii7 passing chord dropped, I, then V7-I. Refrain: IV, I (augmented passing chords on the echoes dropped), V, I, IV, I, V7, I.
